script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Saying the eight hundred were enough to earn Josheb-basshebeth his title adds a reason the passage does not give.
The oven comparison puts the LORD in the role of a bakery appliance, making a joke out of His part in the victory.
Casserole breaks the food rule. It is not in the passage or an answer on this card.
Saying Shammah picks the spot where everybody can see him adds an unsupported reason for his choice.
The passage does not establish that the edge of the field would be safer.
Saying Shammah does not take the road treats the imagined road as a detail of the scene.
David speaks his wish aloud; the passage does not say he sighed. It also says the men broke through the camp, not that they went through its middle.
The passage describes a drink of water, but does not say it was a large amount.
Calling it a quiet moment after a loud trip adds details about both scenes that the passage does not give.
Saying he has only ever had a drawer full of strangers overlooks his six cookie cutter kids and the friends he made in the drawer.
Abner was not Saul's uncle. Ner, Abner's father, was Saul's uncle; Abner was Saul's cousin (1 Samuel 14:50–51).
The closing line about the number sticking on a second hearing is generic and does not add Papa Dorin's personality.
The closing comment about memorable details is generic, especially in a scene with a lion, a pit and snow.
The yard-sale joke treats snatching a weapon and killing the Egyptian as a favorable trade, making light of the violence.
Saying the guard shows up when David appoints Benaiah over it adds an event the passage does not describe.
